takeaway: The coronary sinus receives the small, middle and great cardiac veins. The anterior cardiac veins bypass it and drain directly into the right atrium.

lines.text: Which vein does not drain into the coronary sinus?
The coronary sinus lies in the posterior atrioventricular groove and opens into the right atrium.
It receives the small cardiac vein, which runs with the marginal artery along the inferior border,
the middle cardiac vein, in the inferior interventricular groove,
and the great cardiac vein, in the anterior interventricular groove.
The anterior cardiac veins are not among them: they drain directly into the right atrium.
So the odd one out is the anterior cardiac vein.
lines.say: (laugh) So the odd one out is the anterior cardiac vein.
